title: ruling-door-supersede-path
intention: Give the ruling door a way to retire a MISFILED packet without editing a confirmed record of truth in place.
why: Found by first real use, 2026-08-02. CC misused what_dies (which means the path CEASES TO EXIST) to mean 'the stale claim inside this file dies'; verify caught it in thirty seconds, exactly as designed. But there is no supersede path: open_ruling rewrites the same id with confirmed:false, which would ERASE Akien's act, so the corrected packet had to take a new id and the misfiled one stays on disk, permanently red. The Stop hook now reports it every single turn. A permanent red is noise, and noise gets trained away while still LOOKING like coverage — the same failure this system names elsewhere as coin-toss-red. NOT structural by the 2026-08-02 test: editing lines of code fixes it.
traces_to: Law 7 — errors loud and permanent in records of truth: a misfiled packet must be retired without editing the confirmed record

falsifier.proves_green: proof beside the code, sealed under the tester — SATISFIED 2026-08-02: 23 teeth (6 new, replaying this misfile) green bare and under the tester; VALIDATION appended at cairn/machines/ruling/validations/test_ruling.json
falsifier.proves_red: After the supersede path exists: retire 2026-08-02-three-entry-points-and-structural and confirm that (a) its confirmation_verbatim is still on disk unaltered, and (b) `bin/cmd/ruling --hook` no longer names it. If retiring it requires an in-place edit of the confirmed record, the path is not built. — SATISFIED LIVE 2026-08-02: sha256 of the retired packet identical before and after the act (d094da9a…654b2); hook output empty, exit 0. WHAT AKIEN WAS EXPERIENCING, now gone: every session opened with '/intent was ruled dead and is on disk', reading exactly like his skill being deleted when he had ruled no such thing.
falsifier.horizon: while the hook reds on it every turn — the cost is per-turn, so it compounds. CLOSED 2026-08-02: the per-turn red is gone.
